title: Best Autumn Foliage Spots in Korea 2026: A Fan's Guide
description: Plan your trip to see Korea's stunning autumn foliage in 2026. Discover the best timing and spots for palace colors, mountain hikes, and ginkgo streets.
html:
Plan your trip to see Korea's stunning autumn foliage in 2026. Discover the best timing and spots for palace colors, mountain hikes, and ginkgo streets.

Photo: 정규진 (Korea Tourism Org.) — 전라북도 정읍시 내장동, 내장산국립공원

Autumn in Korea hits different, ngl.

Forget those postcard pics, the real deal is when the whole country turns into a giant mood board. If you're coming for a comeback or just, like, *life*, timing this right is key. We're talking those insane reds and yellows that just make you wanna cry. NGL, I've missed peak foliage by like a week before and it was devastating. So, here’s the lowdown on where to be and when.

Palace Views That Are Actually Worth It

Okay, so everyone hits up Gyeongbokgung, which is gorgeous, duh. But for autumn? You gotta see it framed by the trees. Honestly, Changdeonggung Palace and its Secret Garden (Huwon) is where it’s at. It’s way less crowded and the trees inside are just… immaculate. Seriously, booking the Secret Garden tour is non-negotiable. The autumn colors against the traditional architecture? *Chef’s kiss*.

Changdeonggung Palace (창덕궁) & Secret Garden (후원)

Subway Line 3, Anguk Station, Exit 3. (Approx. 10 min walk). Secret Garden tours run multiple times daily, book online WAY in advance, esp. for fall. Slots are limited! Standard palace entry is ₩3,000, Secret Garden tour is an extra ₩5,000. Worth it. Completely worth it.

The trees here just hit different in October. That deep red maple is unreal.

Mountains for That Epic Fall Hike Vibe

If you're looking for that dramatic, sweeping view, mountains are your move. Seoraksan National Park is the classic, and for good reason. It's like, the OG fall foliage spot. But it gets WILDLY crowded. If you want something a bit more chill, try Naejangsan National Park. It’s famous for its colorful maple leaves lining the paths.

Naejangsan National Park (내장산 국립공원)

Take KTX from Seoul Station to Jeongeup Station (approx. 1.5-2 hours, ₩28,600-₩40,000 depending on seat). From Jeongeup Station, take a local bus or taxi to the park entrance (approx. 30 mins). Peak foliage usually hits mid-to-late October. Park entrance fee is minimal (₩3,000), but cable car is extra (₩10,000 round trip).

The walk from the bus stop to the main temple area is basically a tunnel of red and orange leaves. It’s insane. The cable car gives you a sick panoramic view if you wanna skip the hike up.

Ginkgo Streets That Make You Feel Like You’re in a Drama

Okay, the bright yellow ginkgo trees are iconic. Like, you *will* see them on Instagram and immediately book a flight. Seoul has some legit spots. The area around Seoul Forest is great, but my personal fave is the street along the War Memorial of Korea. It’s huge, lined with ginkgos, and way fewer people than, say, the Olympic Park ginkgo road which can get PACKED.

Ginkgo Street near War Memorial of Korea

Subway Line 4 or 6, Samgakji Station, Exit 1. (Right there). Late October to early November is prime time for the ginkgo. It’s a public street, so free 24/7, but best during daylight hours.

The sheer number of trees is wild. Just walking down the street feels like you’re in a movie scene. It's surprisingly peaceful given how central it is.

When to Actually Go

This is the real tea. Foliage timing depends *heavily* on the year and region. Generally:

  • Mountains (like Seoraksan, Naejangsan): Mid-October is usually the sweet spot.
  • Seoul & Palaces: Late October to early November. The city temps are cooler, and the colors are popping.
  • Ginkgo: Can hang on a bit longer, so early November is still a good bet in Seoul.

My advice? Aim for the last week of October. It gives you the best chance to catch Seoul at peak AND maybe hit the tail end of mountain colors if you venture out. It’s a gamble, but that’s part of the fun, right?

FAQ

Q. How much KRW should I budget for foliage spots?
A. Entrance fees are generally cheap (₩3,000-₩5,000 for palaces/parks). Factor in transport (₩5,000-₩50,000+ depending on KTX) and food. You can easily do a day trip for under ₩50,000 if you're smart about transport and food.

Q. Are there any autumn festivals I should know about?
A. Yes! Many parks and regions have small local festivals, especially around Naejangsan or in areas known for specific trees. Check local tourism sites closer to the date, but don't expect anything as huge as summer festivals.

Q. What should I wear for autumn in Korea?
A. Layers are key! Mornings and evenings can be chilly (around 10-15°C), while afternoons can be pleasant (up to 20°C). Think a light jacket or hoodie over a long-sleeve shirt, comfy walking shoes are a MUST. Scarf and gloves are good for late Oct/early Nov, especially in mountains.
